demo.banner: Demo: nothing you type leaves your browser. Use your own photos.
demo.legal: This deployment is a demonstration with no server and no database behind it. What follows describes the service as it is built, not as this page runs it: here nothing you type is collected or stored, and none of it leaves your browser. The map tiles still come from OpenStreetMap, as described below.
demo.contact: The demonstration has no contact address. Nothing is collected here, so there is nothing to write about.
demo.noWorker: This demo answers its own API calls from a service worker, and this browser did not let it start one. A regular, non-private window should work.

hero.lead: Someone recognises the cat on your street faster than any shelter database will. This is a board for that, and for the shelters rehoming the animals nobody came back for. Moderated before anything goes public.

sections.howLead: Three steps, and a moderator between every listing and the public page.
sections.stepOneBody: A photo and a spot on the map. No name and no number: whoever recognises the animal writes to you through the site.
sections.stepTwoBody: Every listing waits in a queue. Nothing reaches the public map before somebody has looked at the photo.
sections.stepThreeBody: The listing shows on the map for the neighbourhood it belongs to, and a message reaches you by email.

legal.contact: Questions, or a request about your own data:
legal.privacyIntro: A portfolio project with real accounts: if you register you type in a real email address. This says what happens to it. It covers this site and the API behind it, which is where everything is stored.
legal.privacyWhoBody:
One person runs this and answers for the data on it. No company, and no data protection officer, because at this size neither is required. The address at the bottom of this page reaches a human.

Not intended for anyone under 16. If you are under 16, do not create an account here.
legal.privacyWhatBody:
Your email address, to sign you in and to send the confirmation link. Stored lowercased.

Your password, as an argon2 hash. The password itself is never stored and cannot be recovered from the hash.

Your listings: the text you write, the photos, a city and a point on the map.

Messages you write about a listing: emailed to whoever posted it, with your address to reply to, and not kept.

Request logs: IP address, method, path, status and timing. The IP is also what rate limiting counts, held for a minute at a time. Session cookies are stripped before a log line is written.

Reports you file: your account id, the reason and the note.

Moderation decisions: which moderator approved, rejected, edited or deleted which listing, and why. That record holds no personal data of its own.

Nothing for advertising, profiling or analytics. No third-party script, no tracking pixel.
legal.privacyPublicTitle: What is public, and what is not
legal.privacyPublicBody:
Public on an approved listing: the description, the photos, the species, the city, and the location rounded to about a hundred metres.

Not public: anything about the person who posted it. A listing carries no name and no number; people write through the site, the message goes by email, and nobody's address shows until they answer.

Search engines are asked not to index listing pages, in robots.txt and in a header on the page itself.

Some listings come from shelter websites rather than from a person. Those are marked and name the shelter they came from.
legal.privacyBasisBody:
Your account runs the service you asked for: Article 6(1)(b) GDPR.

Publishing a listing is a choice you make one listing at a time and rests on your consent, Article 6(1)(a). Withdrawing it means deleting the listing, which you can do from your listings page at any moment.

Holding listings in a moderation queue, rate limiting and logging who wrote to whom are what keep the board usable and its posters unharvested: legitimate interest, Article 6(1)(f).
legal.privacyThirdBody:
Three processors, each getting only what it needs.

Resend receives your email address to deliver a confirmation or a reset link, and the text of any message you write about a listing.

Railway hosts the API, the database and Redis, so it holds everything at rest.

Cloudflare hosts this site and stores the photos in R2.

One more thing happens in your browser rather than on the server: map tiles come from OpenStreetMap, so their servers see your IP address and the area you are looking at. That happens on any page with a map, with or without an account.

The typefaces are served from this site rather than from Google Fonts, so no font request leaves for a third party.

Nothing is sold, and nothing goes to anybody not on this list, other than to answer a lawful request from an authority.
legal.privacyKeepBody:
Your account: until you delete it.

A rejected listing: 30 days after the decision. Every listing: 180 days after it was posted, and its photos with it. A found animal from last spring is not news, and until it goes it is somebody's street on a public page.

Photos uploaded and never attached to a listing: 24 hours.

Sessions: 30 days, or immediately when you log out or reset your password. Password reset links: one hour. Confirmation links: one day. Rate limiting counters: one minute. Request logs follow the hosting provider's retention.
legal.privacyBrowserTitle: What is stored in your browser
legal.privacyBrowserBody:
Two cookies, access_token and refresh_token, both HttpOnly and both SameSite=Lax. They are what keep you signed in, and they track nothing.

One key in local storage, i18nextLng, remembering whether you chose English or Portuguese.

That is the whole list, and it is why this site has no consent banner: everything on it is strictly necessary or set at your own request. Being exempt from asking is not being exempt from telling, which is what this paragraph is for.

One thing your browser does before anything is sent: a photo you attach is re-encoded here, on your device, which drops the camera metadata including the GPS tag your phone wrote into it. The server strips it again on arrival, so it does not rest on your browser having managed it.
legal.privacyAiTitle: No AI, no automated decisions, no payments
legal.privacyAiBody:
Every listing is read by a person before it appears. Nothing here classifies, scores or ranks you automatically, so Article 22 GDPR does not come into it. No model reads your data, nothing here is generated by one, and nothing is sent to a model provider.

There is no subscription, no paid tier and no card data anywhere in this project.
legal.privacyRightsBody:
Articles 15 to 21 GDPR: a copy of your data, correction, deletion, restriction, objection, and portability.

A copy: your account page has a button for it.

Deletion: the same page. It removes the account, its listings, the photos behind them and every session, immediately and permanently. Two things outlive it: the record of moderation decisions, which names an id and not a person, and any report you filed, which keeps the reason and loses the link to you.

Correction: edit the listing, or write to the address below.

If an answer here is unsatisfactory, the Portuguese supervisory authority is the CNPD, at cnpd.pt.
legal.termsIntro: A short set of rules for a small board. Worth reading once.
legal.termsPostBody:
An animal you found, one you lost, or one looking for a home. One listing per animal.

Not: an animal for sale, a litter being advertised, anything asking for money in exchange for returning an animal, anybody's name, number or address, or a photograph you have no right to use.
legal.termsModerationBody: Every listing waits for a person to read it before it appears. Editing a listing that is already live sends it back to the queue. A rejection comes with a reason where there is one worth giving. The decisions are made by hand and can be wrong; write to the address on the privacy page and it gets looked at again.
legal.termsContactBody: Your listing carries nothing about you. People write to you through the site, the message reaches you by email, and your address stays private until you answer. Writing takes an account of your own and is limited per hour. Using the message form for anything other than the animal ends the account that did it.
legal.termsNoWarrantyBody: This is a side project run by one person in their own time. It can go down, lose data, or stop existing. Listings are written by other people and are checked against the rules above, not for truth. Meet strangers in public places and use your judgement.
legal.termsRemovalBody: You can delete any listing of your own at any time, and its photographs go with it. A listing that breaks the rules is removed without notice. An account that keeps breaking them is closed.
